The ellipse's axes are determined by eigenvalues of the matrix. The set of (x,y) satisfying that is an ellipse (and it's a closed bounded region - because matrix is positive definite if eigenvalues >0). Indeed, symmetric matrix [[2,3],[3,5]]; eigenvalues: solve det[[2-λ,3],[3,5-λ]] = (2-λ)(5-λ) -9 = (10 -7λ + λ^2) -9 = λ^2 -7λ +1 = 0 → λ = [7 ± sqrt(49 -4)]/2 = (7 ± sqrt45)/2 = (7 ± 3*sqrt5)/2.

### Maximum of a linear functional on the ellipse  

For any fixed vector \(c\) the maximum of \(c^{T}v\) subject to \(v^{T}Av=1\) is

\[
\max_{v^{T}Av=1}c^{T}v
    =\sqrt{c^{T}A^{-1}c},
\]

which follows from the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality applied to
\(A^{1/2}v\) and \(A^{-1/2}c\).

Since  

\[
A^{-1}=\frac1{\det A}
\begin{pmatrix}5&-3\\-3&2\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}5&-3\\-3&2\end{pmatrix},
\]

we obtain

\[
\max|x|=\sqrt{(1,0)A^{-1}(1,0)^{T}}=\sqrt{5},\qquad
\max|y|=\sqrt{(0,1)A^{-1}(0,1)^{T}}=\sqrt{2}.
\]

Therefore  

\[
-\sqrt5\le x\le\sqrt5,\qquad
-\sqrt2\le y\le\sqrt2 .
\]

\(x=\pm\sqrt5,\;y=\mp\frac35\sqrt5\).

\(\frac{y^{2}}2=1\) we get
